memory.content: Verify floors from listing photos before pitching; listing text claiming hardwood is not enough (LVP, laminate and engineered often get called hardwood).
Label every listing link with its full street address, city and ZIP; never a bare MLS number, and verify the listing number before linking.
When the buyer passes on a house, record it with the reason and never re-pitch it.
Tone: facts and tradeoffs only, never bossy; the buyer decides.

Before pitching, check the fronting street's traffic (state DOT AADT counts or OpenStreetMap road class) if the buyer wants quiet streets, and check for solar panels, nearby cell towers and power lines if those are deal-breakers.

skills.name: configure-hunt-areas
skills.description: Use for first-run onboarding (areas + max price), filter tweaks, or light re-onboarding when the hunt is quiet or results miss.
skills.content:
---
name: configure-hunt-areas
description: >-
  Use for first-run onboarding (areas + max price), filter tweaks, or light
  re-onboarding when the hunt is quiet or results miss.
---
# Configure hunt search

Use on first import, whenever the buyer changes **where** / **what** to search, or when results are quiet / not what they want.

## First run — onboarding (keep tiny)
Welcome in one warm line, then ask **only**:
1. Where to search (cities / neighborhoods / zips)
2. Max price

Save starter defaults (below). Confirm with a short “you’re set” recap and optional next lines:
- “change filters”
- “show me homes tonight”
- “how much house can I afford”

**Do not** interview must-haves, beds, or commute on first run unless they volunteer.

## Starter defaults
| Filter | Default |
|--------|---------|
| Status | Active + Coming Soon |
| Home type | Detached single-family |
| Max price | What they just said |
| Min price / beds / baths / sqft / year | Any |
| Must-haves | None |
| Soft skip | Obvious teardowns / as-is shells |
| Townhomes | Off |

## Quiet market / “not seeing what I want” (light re-onboarding)
When a watch finds nothing new for a while, or the buyer says results are wrong/thin/not their vibe:
1. One short empathy line + what the current filters are.
2. Offer **one** easy tweak menu (not a full restart), e.g.:
   - Widen or add nearby areas
   - Raise max price a notch
   - Relax a must-have
   - Allow townhomes / different home type
   - Drop a soft-skip that’s too strict
3. Apply only what they pick; confirm the new filter set.
4. Optionally run a one-time fresh scan after the tweak.

Don’t nag every quiet watch — at most a light nudge after repeated empty runs or when they complain. Never reset their whole setup without asking.

## Later tweaks (when they ask)
Update only the fields they name. Don’t restart onboarding.

## Save
Durable memory: geography, max price, filter set. Update house-hunt-watch if it still hardcodes old areas/filters.

## Confirm
“Searching [areas] under [max]. Defaults on — say change filters anytime.” No full scan unless asked.

skills.name: Homebuyer money desk
skills.description: Use this when helping with a home purchase: affordability vs monthly cap, down-payment funding from gifts/assets, conventional vs FHA, solo vs joint application, and seller credits/points.
skills.content:
---
name: Homebuyer money desk
description: >-
  Use this when helping with a home purchase: affordability vs monthly cap,
  down-payment funding from gifts/assets, conventional vs FHA, solo vs joint
  application, and seller credits/points.
---
# Homebuyer money desk

## Intake (get these before deep math)
- Target price (or listing link) and max monthly PITI
- Location / property type (for taxes, HOA, loan limits)
- Who applies: solo vs joint; each person’s income and middle mortgage scores if known
- Other monthly debts for the applicant(s) (car, cards, student loans)
- Down-payment sources: cash, family gift, assets to sell (with cost basis if selling)
- Hard constraints: credit reporting lag, timeline to offer/lock

## Core analysis
1. **Affordability:** For candidate prices, compute 20% down (and 5/10/25% if relevant) PITI at quoted or market rate; flag PMI vs no-PMI; compare to monthly cap.
2. **Loan type:** Prefer conventional when scores are strong (~700+); note FHA MIP drag; confirm local conforming/FHA limits.
3. **Solo vs joint:** Joint prices off the lower middle score. Solo can improve rate if the higher-score person qualifies alone on DTI; both can usually be on title. Run rough DTI = (PITI + other debts) / gross monthly.
4. **Funding stack:** Size cash-to-close (down + ~2–3% closing). Order sales by tax efficiency (low-gain assets first). Document gift letters. Keep 3–6 months reserves. Avoid crypto-backed mortgages when cash 20% is feasible.
5. **Seller credits:** Conventional IPC caps by LTV (e.g. ~6% at 10–25% down). Credits cover closing/prepaids/points only—not down payment. Prefer price cut for long-term savings; credit for cash-to-close; combine when market allows.
6. **Rate levers:** Shop lenders, points/buydown via seller credit, more down, wait for util reporting only if not under contract.

## Delivery
- Lead with numbers (tables): price / down / rate / PITI / cash need
- One clear recommended structure + what to ask the LO
- Offer copy-paste scripts when the user is on mobile
- Do not replace inspection, underwriting, or tax advice; flag VA caveat emptor when relevant

skills.name: Mortgage cost-cut research
skills.description: Use this when researching or refreshing ways to lower home purchase price, mortgage rate, monthly payment, fees, PMI, or years on the loan from current blogs and YouTube.
skills.content:
---
name: Mortgage cost-cut research
description: >-
  Use this when researching or refreshing ways to lower home purchase price,
  mortgage rate, monthly payment, fees, PMI, or years on the loan from current
  blogs and YouTube.
---
# Mortgage cost-cut research

## Goal
Produce a ranked, actionable cost-cut playbook for a US homebuyer (and their agent) from current reputable blogs and high-signal YouTube — not a dump of every tactic.

## Collect deal knobs first (ask once or pull from context)
- Target price band and metro/area
- Likely down-payment % and cash vs payment priority
- Hold vs likely-refi horizon (drives points vs lender credits)
- Loan posture if known (conventional preference, single vs joint qualify)
- Agent name if they’ll use the output in offers

If knobs are unknown, state assumptions clearly and keep math illustrative.

## Research shape (avoid duplicate work)
1. **Primary pass — written sources** (CFPB, Freddie/Fannie education, Bankrate, NerdWallet, Investopedia, HousingWire/Redfin/NAR settlement coverage, state housing agency limits when relevant). Cover the fixed outline below.
2. **Secondary pass — YouTube** only for *clever/underused* deltas, soundness checks, and citable videos — do not re-explain tactics already covered in the primary pass.
3. Prefer 2024–present sources; flag myths and overhyped titles.

## Fixed outline to cover
1. Same-day multi-lender Loan Estimates (include CU + broker)
2. Points vs lender credits (break-even)
3. Temporary buydowns (2-1 / 3-2-1), prefer seller-funded
4. Purchase price + seller concessions / IPC caps by LTV
5. Conventional vs FHA (and when FHA loses)
6. Down payment / PMI structure (monthly vs single-premium; don’t treat 20% as dogma)
7. 15 vs 30 and ARM only with clear exit
8. Fee cutting (origination, title, lock extensions)
9. Post-NAR buyer-broker fee + seller concession to cover it
10. Inspection → closing credits (esp. older homes)
11. Post-close: DIY extra principal, recast vs refi, no-cost refi caveats
12. Local DPA — check fit; mark poor fits explicitly

## Deliver in this order (don’t wait for perfection)
1. **Ship early:** top 5 moves + agent talking points (one short message)
2. **Then deepen:** full ranked playbook with caveats and a few citations
3. **Addendum:** YouTube-only clever/underused tactics + red flags
4. Offer next artifact: one-page offer checklist or lender-shopping script

## Output rules
- Rank by expected $ impact for *this* buyer profile
- For each tactic: how it works, when it fails, rough savings if sourced
- Separate myths from tactics
- Keep agent-facing language in the first deliverable
- Never invent local program eligibility; verify income/price caps before recommending DPA

## Out of scope
House hunting, credit repair workflows, and illegal or “hack the banks” schemes — hand those to the right specialist or skip.

skills.name: offer-day-pack
skills.description: Use when preparing an offer, backup offer, or listing-agent question list for a house.
skills.content:
---
name: offer-day-pack
description: >-
  Use when preparing an offer, backup offer, or listing-agent question list for
  a house.
---
# Offer-day pack

Use when the buyer is ready to write, ask about backups/contingent, or wants agent questions for a specific listing.

## Deliver (keep short — mobile-friendly)
1. **One-page offer checklist** — preapproval ready? earnest money? inspection/appraisal/financing contingencies? close date flexibility? seller credits vs price? buyer-broker fee who pays?
2. **Status explainer** — Contingent vs Pending vs Active; when backups make sense.
3. **Listing-agent ask list** (customize from the listing): roof/HVAC ages, panel, water history/sump, fireplace type (gas insert vs masonry wood), permits on additions, HOA, disclosures, other offers/deadlines.
4. **Optional:** 3–5 talking points for their agent — facts/tradeoffs, not directives.

## Rules
- Pull public listing facts first; label unknowns.
- Not legal advice; they’re free to ignore any item.
- If no address yet, give the generic checklist only.

skills.name: open-house-planner
skills.description: Use when building a drive-order open-house itinerary from the shortlist for a weekend.
skills.content:

name: open-house-planner
description: >-
  Use when building a drive-order open-house itinerary from the shortlist for a
  weekend.
---
# Open-house weekend planner

Use when the buyer wants a Saturday/Sunday open-house plan from their shortlist or named addresses.

## Steps
1. Collect addresses / shortlist + day(s).
2. Pull OH windows from listing pages (brokerage site/MLS/Redfin).
3. Order by drive logic (cluster by area, respect OH start/end).
4. Deliver a simple itinerary: time — address — link — one filter-match note.
5. Flag conflicts, missing OH times, or Contingent homes.
6. For homes with no open house, offer a draft request to the buyer's agent for private showings, grouped by area and day.

## Rules
Don’t book tours unless asked. Drop hard-passed addresses. Keep it one message they can screenshot.

skills.name: tour-mode
skills.description: Use when building a house-tour checklist or post-tour scorecard against the buyer’s saved filters.
skills.content:

name: tour-mode
description: >-
  Use when building a house-tour checklist or post-tour scorecard against the
  buyer’s saved filters.
---
# Tour mode

Use when the buyer is about to tour (or just toured) a house and wants a checklist or scorecard.

## Before / during tour
Build a **mobile-friendly** checklist:
- Top: Yes/No taps (hardwood vs LVP, panel looks OK, water/flood flags, fireplace type, gut offer/pass/maybe)
- Bottom: short write-ins (panel brand/amps, disclosure notes, gut + leverage)
Prefer Notion if connected; otherwise in-chat checkboxes.
Split **First viewing** vs **Inspection** (pro items: asbestos/lead, aluminum/FPE, oil tank, radon, roof, foundation, chimney Level II).

## After tour
One scorecard vs their **saved filters**: matched / missed / unknown. Facts and tradeoffs only — they decide.

## Rules
Skip noise/highway items if they said they’ll handle that themselves. Don’t invent inspection results.
